passage:
A museum displayed a star chart made long before modern telescopes. The stars were drawn by hand, with animals and heroes connecting them.
Students compared it with a modern sky map. The old chart was less exact, but more artistic. It showed how people used stories to remember the night sky.
The guide said astronomy began not only with instruments, but with patient watching.
Students looked at the chart and imagined people standing outside centuries ago, trying to make order out of darkness.
The stars had not changed much, but human understanding had. A chart can show both the sky and the mind of the people who mapped it.
